questions.stem: Dans une note de groupe, what does adaptation imply?

options.text: Changing to fit a new context.

questions.explanation: Adaptation means changing to fit a new context. Option B ("Changing to fit a new context.") is the key because it satisfies that rule. Option A is tempting but wrong: ignores change. Option C is tempting but wrong: overstates change. Option D is tempting but wrong: confuses with reproduction.

questions.topic: Dating a charter from its seal and regnal year
questions.learningObjective: Date a charter from its seal and regnal year
questions.stem: A historian examines a medieval charter bearing a seal and a regnal-year formula. What can these features provide?

options.text: Only the modern calendar date matters.
options.misconception: Insists on a modern date the charter lacks
Denies that seals convey any dating clue

options.text: The seal and regnal year fix the date.

questions.explanation: The seal together with the regnal year are standard tools for dating medieval charters, so option D is correct. Option A dismisses regnal years, B insists only a modern date counts, and C wrongly denies that seals carry date information.
questions.hint: Both features help place the charter in time.

questions.topic: A textbook claim and what the evidence reverses
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a textbook claim against evidence

stimulus.body: The study group revision contrasts a textbook claim with new evidence that reverses it.

questions.stem: Dans une note de groupe, what should a reader do when evidence reverses a textbook claim?

options.text: Revise the claim in light of evidence.
Keep the textbook as absolute truth.

questions.explanation: Evidence that reverses a claim should lead to revising it. Option B ("Revise the claim in light of evidence.") is the key because it satisfies that rule. Option A is tempting but wrong: denies revision. Option C is tempting but wrong: uncritical stance. Option D is tempting but wrong: overreaction.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Reading a chancery date
questions.learningObjective: Read a chancery date
questions.stem: A document scholar sees a royal charter dated by a king's regnal year and a saint's feast. What dating system is being used?

options.misconception: Claims the charter has no date at all

options.text: It dates by regnal year and feast day.

options.misconception: Invents a record of only the hour

questions.explanation: Dating by a ruler's regnal year and a feast day is the chancery convention for medieval documents, so option C is correct. Option A says documents lack dates, B assumes modern months appear, and D invents an hour-only record; all miss the regnal-and-feast convention.
questions.hint: Identify the system based on reigns and feast days.
